author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-18 on prometheus/prometheus@6063ce7 (727 Go files, 370k lines) against an INDEPENDENT go/ast oracle - a real Go program using the standard parser, not a second tree-sitter pass, so it is a second opinion rather than a mirror.

The oracle agreed exactly on the things that matter most: 4680 funcs and 4972 methods, 9652 total, and memway found 9652 - a 100% match, name for name, file for file. Types were 1569 of 1578.

All nine missing are TYPE ALIASES - `type X = Y` - and walk() registers type definitions but not aliases. The consequence is worse than nine absent names, because METHODS DECLARED ON AN ALIAS ARE STILL INDEXED. discovery/xds/kuma.go declares `type KumaSDConfig = SDConfig` and five methods on it, and the map holds all five:

  discovery.xds.kuma.KumaSDConfig.Name
  discovery.xds.kuma.KumaSDConfig.NewDiscoverer
  discovery.xds.kuma.KumaSDConfig.NewDiscovererMetrics
  discovery.xds.kuma.KumaSDConfig.SetDirectory
  discovery.xds.kuma.KumaSDConfig.UnmarshalYAML

...with no entity for KumaSDConfig itself. The qualname prefix resolves to nothing, so the tree has children whose parent does not exist. `memway show <repo> KumaSDConfig` answers "no entity matches 'KumaSDConfig'" and then lists KumaSDConfig.Name under "closest:" - the name is visibly present in the answer that denies it. Two of the nine are public API (KumaSDConfig, web.PrometheusVersion) and one is a package's central type (util/compression.Type).

This is memway-tasks#12's family - a Go node type the walk does not handle - but NOT the same failure: #12 is about a grammar rename silently dropping 422/648 entities, and this is a shape never handled at all. Both are found the same way, which is the argument for the finding: an independent oracle on an unfamiliar repo, not a fixture.

NOT FIXED as of 0.57.2, recorded deliberately. Whether an alias should be its own coordinate is a real design question - it names an existing type rather than declaring a new one - but the current behaviour is not a considered answer to it, because it leaves parented methods pointing at nothing. Whatever is decided, that inconsistency is the part that is wrong.

For the record from the same run: 12,987 entities and 30,914 edges in 28s cold, 6.8s incremental with 12,987 memoized and 0 recomputed. Ambiguity at Go scale behaves: `String` names 132 entities and is reported as ambiguous, `Close` 86, `Append` 36, and the unresolved-reference counter reads 0 on Head.Appender and scrapePool.sync.

author: cli
text:
Re-read at 0.57.2, and this coordinate now carries the fix for the defect reported below it. The Go parser records via_attr and bare on every call edge: `x.foo()` parses as a selector_expression, `foo()` as a plain identifier, and the difference is what lets the resolver refuse a builtin call landing on a same-named method. prometheus: memChunk.len went from 1,619 incoming call edges to 13, and the 13 are real receiver calls.

GoParser also declares builtin_names - the Go spec's predeclared function identifiers. Not derivable from a Python process, so it is a literal list, and its source is named in the comment beside it.

The TYPE ALIAS defect recorded below is UNCHANGED and still open: `type X = Y` is not registered, while methods declared on the alias are, so five entities sit parented on a KumaSDConfig that has no entity.
